title: Chest Pain Imaging Appropriateness Guidance
recommendation_blocks: Select imaging based on the working clinical question rather than ordering broad imaging panels for all chest-pain presentations.
Confirm hemodynamic stability, ECG findings, and pulmonary embolism risk before escalating to CT angiography.
Use the lowest-risk study that answers the immediate clinical question and avoids avoidable contrast or radiation exposure.

title: Incidental Lung Nodule Follow-up Guidance
recommendation_blocks: Document nodule size, risk context, and the recommended follow-up interval in a structured way.
Trigger follow-up tracking rather than relying on a free-text recommendation alone.
Escalate sooner when morphology or patient risk context suggests a higher likelihood of malignancy.

title: Suspected Fracture Imaging Guidance
recommendation_blocks: Start with targeted plain radiography for most suspected fractures unless mechanism or instability justifies advanced imaging first.
Escalate to CT when complex anatomy, occult fracture concern, or operative planning requires better bony detail.
Pair imaging requests with the precise injury question so protocol selection is clinically aligned.
